whole_file_writer_crosscheck.observed_code: Both methods use new StreamWriter(filePath) and CsvWriter.WriteRecords(Instance.layers).
whole_file_writer_crosscheck.interpretation: For a given existing path, the default StreamWriter constructor truncates/overwrites the file and then serializes the whole layer collection; a reader can encounter an empty or partial rewrite window. Such a race does not require waiting for the next completed layer or an Excel step lasting 58 seconds.
qualifications: The exact source version of the running BJT binary is unverified.
With blank filePath these methods generate a DateTime.Now filename; their definitions alone do not establish per-layer call schedule or path reuse.
This is a plausible race mechanism, not proof of the original incident timing or of actual Excel latency.

independent_synthetic_rewrite_probe.scope: Production parser/adapter with temporary synthetic CSV and mocked UI, no next completed layer required.
independent_synthetic_rewrite_probe.observed: Empty and partial same-layer rewrite windows both produced ObservationSuspended with zero native apply, Save and settings recovery. Restored layer/temperature remained readable.
independent_synthetic_rewrite_probe.eligibility_limit: After empty restore the observation_key can remain None because generation/freshness fencing is conservative. Readable display does not imply a row is eligible for calculation or Save.
independent_synthetic_rewrite_probe.initial_assertion_limit: An initial reviewer assertion that restoration always yields a valid observation_key was too strong and failed for the empty-window fixture. That assertion is not treated as a product failure or a passed test; the raw observed result is preserved.

limits: Native UI checks use synthetic Windows fixtures and temporary files; they do not validate the live BJT application or physical M1/S3 equipment.
Excel COM is not registered in the runner; no real workbook COM speed or end-to-end calculation latency was measured.
The 92.986 ms measurement is a 32 MiB hash guard benchmark on one CI run, not Excel or device latency.
CSV-only checks cannot prove physical sensor freshness, lamp/PLC behavior or long-run thermal stability.
The original incident mechanism and why BinderJet stopped before 259 remain unconfirmed.
Release readiness remains false; no EXE release, distribution, equipment application or final control approval was requested or performed.
